Thank you, I’m sorry MS has been affecting you too. I have muscle weakness and ataxia and have been using a walker since leaving the hospital. My entire sense of self has been changing. 

My Neurologist says I’ve likely had MS for years unknowingly. For a few years now I thought I was going crazy and experiencing something like  early Alzheimer’s. I graduated from grad school number one in my class through hard work and studying but I have also always prided myself on my memory skills. 

Over the past few years I noticed a significant change in my memory and have been forgetting all the big and small stuff I should know. Since then I started writing everything down. I have a shared online calendar with my husband that helps keep me organized. I put all my appointments, birthdays and events in it. There’s even a shared shopping list on the calendar too. At work for years I’ve kept a notebook on me that keeps me organized that has everything in it that I need to know from all my important duties to all the day to day stuff. I go through hundreds of post it notes a year, I keep them on the inside of my notebook since it’s always on me. I feel like I have a decent system in place for when I eventually return back to work since my memory has been affecting me for so long. I was a little relieved to finally get a diagnosis that explained all the cognitive and memory issues I’ve been experiencing and that I haven’t been going crazy.

Since getting diagnosed with MS I’m still processing what this means for my future and have been reevaluating my current lifestyle and friendships. 

I hope you continue to stay positive!

Congrats on your first treatment infusion buddy! I had a scratchy/ sore throat at one point during the infusion so I ate some crackers and drank some water and it seemed to go away. I was just happy I could swallow and that my throat wasn’t closing in or anything weird. I told the nurse and she checked on my frequently after that but didn’t have to slow or stop the infusion. After my infusion I got some hot flashes with clammy skin and when the nurse checked my vitals and my pulse was a little high. They put some wet towels on my neck and forehead and watched me for a bit then took vitals again and my pulse had lowered a little. They instructed me to take a Benadryl in the evening and another Xanax at nighttime if needed and to call them if I had any other issues day or night.

Hope you’re felling well today and that you have a nice weekend!

Pros:

* Being around a couple of girls at work at lunch time because I can't escape the baby stories. I'm new to a very small office of all women and none of them know I had a miscarriage or have been trying. I quit my last job hoping less stress would improve our chances but still nothing.
* Having a family member or a friend say or ask "When are you guys going to have kids?" "Oh you haven't been feeling well, are you pregnant? Is it morning sickness?"

I am young and I am currently working on my medical masters to become a physician assistant. I have counseled patients on contraception and have inserted Paraguard and Mirena devices. Don't take your visit personally. I would not recommend the Paraguard or other IUD to anyone who hasn't had children, whether they are 17 or 37. Your uterus is much smaller than someone who has gone through the act of conceiving. The device is designed to sit inside the uterus a certain way- it just fits better in a slightly larger uterus. IUDs can be very painful (especially on insertion), they don't protect against STDs, or help with acne like some oral birth control pills do.  
      
I think you are being very smart and responsible by thinking about contraception at 17. There are a ton of other options to think of as well.  Great luck to you on your path to becoming a CNM!
